faqs.q: Which sticker material works best for general everyday use?
faqs.a: Premium vinyl is the all-purpose choice. It is durable, waterproof and UV-resistant, which makes it a safe pick for product labels, laptops, water bottles and anything that will see daily wear.

faqs.q: When should I choose clear vinyl over premium white vinyl?
faqs.a: Choose clear vinyl when the surface should show through, such as a window, glass jar or clear bottle. On dark surfaces, white ink is required behind the artwork so the design stays visible.

faqs.q: Why do colors look different on holographic vinyl stickers?
faqs.a: Holographic vinyl has a foil base that shifts with the light, so printed colors can appear different from how they look on white vinyl. Your digital proof helps you judge the effect before printing.

faqs.q: Is metallic vinyl suitable for detailed full-color sticker artwork?
faqs.a: Metallic vinyl is not suited to complex full-color designs. It works best for gold, silver and chrome effects on luxury packaging and branding, where simpler artwork lets the metallic finish stand out.

faqs.q: Where do white paper stickers work best compared with vinyl?
faqs.a: White paper suits indoor use, packaging and budget-conscious projects. It is not waterproof and will degrade with moisture, so choose vinyl for anything that will get wet or go outside.

faqs.q: What colors can glow-in-the-dark sticker material produce?
faqs.a: The glow color of glow-in-the-dark material is limited to green or yellow. Plan your artwork around that, and use it for designs where the glowing effect matters more than a wide color range.

faqs.q: What is reflective vinyl sticker material best used for?
faqs.a: Reflective vinyl is a high-visibility material made for safety uses, vehicles and outdoor applications where a sticker needs to be seen clearly when light hits it.

faqs.q: What goes wrong when the wrong sticker material is chosen?
faqs.a: The wrong material can lead to stickers that peel, fade or fail to stick properly. Matching the material to where the sticker will be used is one of the most important decisions in any order.

faqs.q: How does the material comparison chart help me pick a sticker?
faqs.a: The comparison chart puts the materials side by side, so you can weigh properties, available finishes and unsuitable uses for vinyl, clear, holographic, metallic, paper, reflective and glow material at a glance.

faqs.q: Can your team recommend a sticker material for my project?
faqs.a: Yes. Tell us how and where you will use your stickers and our team will recommend the best material. You can get a free quote with material advice in one request.

faqs.q: Which sticker shape suits wine and beverage labels best?
faqs.a: An oval shape works well for wine labels. It is softer than a rectangle and more formal than a circle, which gives bottles a refined, classic look.

faqs.q: When should I choose a rectangle shape for custom stickers?
faqs.a: Rectangle is the standard label shape and the practical pick for product information and address labels, where you need room for text, ingredients or shipping details in a clean layout.

faqs.q: Is standard lamination included on vinyl sticker orders?
faqs.a: Yes. Standard laminate is included on all vinyl orders. It protects the print against water, UV exposure and scratches, so colors stay sharp through everyday handling and weather.

faqs.q: When do custom stickers need a heavy-duty laminate?
faqs.a: Heavy-duty laminate adds an extra-thick protective layer for extreme outdoor or industrial applications, such as equipment, machinery or stickers that face constant abrasion and harsh weather.

faqs.q: Can paper stickers be ordered without any laminate?
faqs.a: Yes. The no-laminate option leaves paper stickers without a protective coating. It is meant for indoor use only, since uncoated paper is not built to handle water or sun.

faqs.q: How do I request Pantone spot color matching on a sticker order?
faqs.a: Specify your Pantone PMS code when you order. Spot color matching is used for brand-critical colors that need exact reproduction, rather than the standard digital CMYK process.

faqs.q: What is white ink printing used for on clear stickers?
faqs.a: White ink creates opaque white areas on transparent and holographic materials. It is used when parts of a clear or holographic sticker need solid white elements or need to stay visible on darker surfaces.

faqs.q: Can I add embossing or foil stamping to sticker labels?
faqs.a: Yes. Embossing and foil stamping create raised or metallic foil elements for premium packaging labels and certificates. See our embossed gold foil stickers for one example.

faqs.q: What printing method is standard for full-color custom stickers?
faqs.a: Digital CMYK printing is our standard process for full-color stickers. It produces sharp, vibrant colors with photographic quality at any quantity, from small runs to large orders.

faqs.q: Which sticker shapes suit rewards, seals and seasonal promotions?
faqs.a: Star shapes are a fun choice for rewards, promotions and seasonal events, while circle stickers are a classic fit for seals and logo stickers. Die cut follows your artwork for anything more distinctive.

faqs.a: Start with the material guide, because material decides whether a sticker lasts years outdoors or peels within weeks. Read how to choose the right sticker material first.

faqs.q: How do the sticker blog guides connect to ordering custom stickers?
faqs.a: Each guide links to the related sticker products it discusses, so you can move from reading about a material, cut or finish straight to the product that uses it and request a quote.

faqs.q: What resolution should raster sticker artwork be saved at?
faqs.a: Raster files need at least 300 DPI at the final print size, and 300 to 600 DPI is recommended for photos and gradients. Screen-resolution images of 72 to 96 DPI, including screenshots, are not acceptable.

faqs.q: Should sticker artwork files be set up in CMYK or RGB?
faqs.a: Set all print files up in CMYK. RGB colors are converted to CMYK during production, which can cause color shifts, so working in CMYK from the start gives you more predictable results.

faqs.q: How much bleed should I add to sticker artwork files?
faqs.a: Add 0.125 inch of bleed on all sides so no white edges appear after cutting, and keep text and logos at least 0.125 inch inside the edge, within the safe zone.

faqs.q: How should I name the die cut line layer in my file?
faqs.a: Put the cut line on a separate spot color layer named CutContour or Die Line, set to overprint. Offset it 0.125 inch from your design edge so all artwork stays visible after cutting.

faqs.q: Why should fonts be outlined before sending sticker artwork?
faqs.a: Outlining fonts converts text to paths, which prevents font substitution when we open your file. In Illustrator, select all text, then choose Type and Create Outlines before saving.

faqs.q: What is the smallest text size that prints clearly on stickers?
faqs.a: Keep text at 6pt or larger to stay readable, and use 8pt or more where you can. Avoid very thin or hairline font weights at small sizes, as they can break up in print.

faqs.q: How should black text and large black areas be set up?
faqs.a: Set black text to 100 K only rather than rich black for crisp edges. For large solid black areas, use rich black built from C60, M40, Y40 and K100 for a deeper result.

faqs.q: How thin can details be in die cut sticker shapes?
faqs.a: Avoid extremely thin cuts under 1/8 inch, since they may not cut cleanly, and keep detail paths in intricate shapes at a stroke width of at least 2pt. This matters most on custom die cut stickers.

faqs.q: How can I send large sticker artwork files to your team?
faqs.a: Upload your file directly through the quote form on any product page, or share it through a Dropbox, Google Drive or WeTransfer link in your message to our team.

faqs.q: Will your design team fix problems in my sticker artwork?
faqs.a: Our design team reviews artwork for free and contacts you about any issues before printing. Basic file preparation, color conversions and file checks cost nothing, and more complex design work can be discussed with the team.

faqs.q: When is it worth choosing something other than standard vinyl stickers?

/blog/die-cut-vs-kiss-cut-stickers/.h2: More Questions About Die-Cut and Kiss-Cut

faqs.q: Can a kiss-cut sticker backing carry my logo or instructions?
faqs.a: Yes. Because a kiss-cut sticker sits on a larger backing sheet, there is room on that backing for branding, instructions or a logo, which works well for packaging inserts and sticker packs.

faqs.q: When should I choose die-cut stickers for a logo design?
faqs.a: Choose die-cut when the shape itself is the statement, such as a logo sticker for laptops or a character cutout. The sticker is cut to your outline and looks like it has no sticker edge.

faqs.q: What is the actual cutting difference between die-cut and kiss-cut?
faqs.a: A die-cut sticker is cut through both the printed vinyl and the paper backing along your design outline. A kiss-cut sticker is cut through the top vinyl layer only, leaving the backing intact.

faqs.q: Does kiss-cut protect delicate points on intricate sticker designs?
faqs.a: Yes. Kiss-cut keeps thin elements and delicate points supported on the backing until the sticker is used, which also makes small or intricate shapes easier to peel and apply cleanly.

faqs.q: Can a brand use both die-cut and kiss-cut stickers together?
faqs.a: Yes, and many brands do: die-cut for hero logo stickers and kiss-cut for multi-design sets. Start with our custom die-cut sticker shapes for the hero design.

faqs.q: Why do some waterproof stickers still fail when used outdoors?
faqs.a: Most failures come from a missing protective layer. The vinyl may resist water, but without a laminate and UV-resistant inks, sunlight fades the ink over a single hot season.

faqs.q: Does wiping a surface with alcohol help outdoor stickers last longer?
faqs.a: Yes. A quick alcohol wipe removes oils and dust before applying, which dramatically improves how long an outdoor sticker stays put, especially on glass, painted metal and hard plastic.

faqs.q: What four parts make up a properly built outdoor sticker?
faqs.a: A durable outdoor sticker combines waterproof vinyl face stock, UV-resistant inks, a laminate layer against scratches and sun, and a weather-rated adhesive that holds through temperature swings.

faqs.q: Which adhesive should outdoor stickers use in changing weather?
faqs.a: Use a weather-rated permanent adhesive. Heat, cold and moisture all stress the bond outdoors, and a standard indoor adhesive is more likely to lift as temperatures change.

faqs.q: What are the best uses for laminated outdoor vinyl stickers?
faqs.a: With the right build they handle vehicle decals, bumper stickers, cooler and hard-hat labels, outdoor equipment, signage and window graphics. See our custom car stickers and decals for vehicle use.

faqs.q: Where can stickers be used across a product packaging unboxing?
faqs.a: Use seal stickers on box flaps or mailers, product labels on jars, bottles and pouches, thank-you or logo stickers inside the box, and on-brand address and shipping labels on the outside.

faqs.q: Why do small brands use stickers before fully printed packaging?
faqs.a: Printing on boxes and mailers is expensive and slow to change. Stickers let a brand ship in plain, affordable packaging and still look polished, and they can be swapped for a new product or season.

faqs.q: How do consistent stickers help a small brand look established?
faqs.a: Using the same logo sticker, seal and label style on every order trains customers to recognize you instantly, which makes a small, home-run operation look like a professional one.

faqs.q: Why do food and beauty labels need oil-resistant sticker stock?
faqs.a: Food, beauty and bath products get handled often and stored in humid places, so waterproof, oil-resistant stocks keep labels readable and stuck down where paper labels would smudge or peel.

faqs.q: Can a single product label replace a printed box panel?
faqs.a: Yes. A well-made label can carry the required information and act as a designed brand asset at the same time, replacing a printed panel. Browse our custom packaging labels for options.

faqs.q: Which sticker finish photographs best for social media product shots?
faqs.a: Glossy stickers photograph bright and saturated, which is a plus for social and product shots. Be aware that gloss can show glare under direct light, so angle your lighting with care.

faqs.q: Does a glossy sticker finish cause glare under direct light?
faqs.a: Yes, glare under direct light is one trade-off of a glossy finish, along with fingerprints showing more readily. A matte finish resists glare if the sticker will be viewed under bright lights.

faqs.q: Should I order finish samples before committing to a full sticker run?
faqs.a: If you are unsure, order a small sample of two finishes on your actual artwork before committing to a full run. Seeing them side by side is the quickest way to decide.

faqs.q: Which kinds of brands suit a matte finish over glossy?
faqs.a: Matte suits premium, minimal and lifestyle brands, and it is common on beauty, wellness and boutique products. Its smooth, non-reflective surface reads as refined and has a pleasant tactile feel.

faqs.q: How does a holographic sticker finish look in changing light?
faqs.a: Holographic stock shifts through rainbow colors as it catches the light, giving a premium, hard-to-counterfeit shimmer for packaging, events and collectibles. Explore custom holographic sticker printing for these runs.
